Theme

Kitchen, meals & drinks

amphora noun

also wine jar, two-handled jar, storage jar, jar of wine

classical

Plaut. Cas. 121: dabitur tibi amphora ūna et ūna sēmita
Cato Agr. 113.2: amphorās implēre (Lewis & Short)

amphora, amphorae f.

noun, first declension

a clay jar with two handles, for wine, oil and the like

Greek ἀμφορεύς. Also a liquid measure.

Other words

  • cadus, cadī m. — a large jar, above all for wine

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Amph. 429: Cadus erat vīnī, inde implēvī hirneam.; Verg. A. 1.195 (Lewis & Short)

    Greek κάδος.

Examples

  • dabitur tibi amphora ūna et ūna sēmita, fōns ūnus, ūnum ahēnum et octō dōlia

    you’ll be given one jar and one path, one spring, one copper and eight vatsPlaut. Cas. 121–122

  • Cadus erat vīnī, inde implēvī hirneam.

    There was a jar of wine; I filled a jug from it.Plaut. Amph. 429

See also jar, urn, wine, bottle, barrel.

SourcesLewis & Short: amphora · Lewis & Short: cadus

Plautus, Amphitruo 429; Casina 121–122.
